title: Three-Act Structure
summary: Classical three-act structure with three required major turns: inciting incident, midpoint twist, and climax.

beats.label: Act One — Setup
beats.summary: Establishes protagonist, world, and status quo. Plants what will pay off later.

beats.label: Inciting Incident
beats.summary: The event that disrupts the protagonist's world and demands a response.

beats.label: First Plot Point
beats.summary: The protagonist commits to the journey. Act One closes; Act Two begins.

beats.label: Act Two — Confrontation
beats.summary: Rising obstacles. The protagonist tries and fails, learning along the way.

beats.label: Midpoint Twist
beats.summary: A revelation or reversal that recasts the protagonist's quest.

beats.label: Second Plot Point
beats.summary: The protagonist receives the final piece needed to confront the antagonist.

beats.label: Act Three — Resolution
beats.summary: The protagonist executes a new plan and the conflict resolves.

beats.label: Climax
beats.summary: The decisive confrontation. Stakes peak. The protagonist wins or loses definitively.
